summary.text: A 48-year-old man with hereditary hearing loss, dyslipidemia, well-controlled hypertension and color vision deficiency had an upper respiratory infection and was prescribed methylprednisolone and a 6-day course of azithromycin; after completing the course he developed blurred vision in both eyes, headache and eye pain. A day after symptom onset an ophthalmologist found count-fingers acuity OD and hand-motion acuity OS, optic disc edema and a Roth spot OS; brain MRI the morning after onset was normal.

A day later he was admitted to an outside hospital, where repeat MRI showed thickening and perineural enhancement along both optic nerves, left greater than right, and he was started on antibiotics, acetazolamide and IV methylprednisolone before transfer 3 days later. On admission he reported subjective improvement and had visual acuity 20/25 OD and count fingers OS; examination also showed a left RAPD, bilateral disc edema worse OS, peripapillary hemorrhages OS, and intraretinal hemorrhages and Roth spots. Serum MOG IgG was positive at 1:1,000 and CSF showed an elevated cell count with negative infectious studies.

PET/CT and body CT were negative for occult malignancy. The final diagnosis was bilateral MOG-associated optic neuritis with intraretinal hemorrhages and Roth spots. He received three further days of IV methylprednisolone, an oral prednisone taper and five sessions of plasmapheresis, and was discharged with visual acuity 20/20 OD and 20/30 OS.

At 6 weeks after discharge his acuity was 20/20 OU; follow-up findings included a persistent left RAPD and resolution of the retinal hemorrhages and Roth spots. At 3 months after the initial hospitalization he had a mild recurrence of symptoms after a recent decrease in prednisone dosage, the steroid taper was slowed because of continued symptoms, and the serum MOG IgG titer had decreased to 1:100. At the 8-month follow-up he had finished the prednisone taper, was largely symptom-free, and OCT showed progressive thinning of the RNFL and ganglion cell complex.
